message:
test(update): drive the owner decision through real processes, both ways

The owner comparison had unit coverage only. What was missing is what the
processes do when it goes each way, and the two endings are supposed to look
nothing alike from outside: one leaves a worker holding a credential, the
other leaves a bootstrap that gave up and no worker at all.

Five cases through the real chain -- unchanged, the same account signed out
and back in, a different account on the same server, signed out entirely,
and the server changed. Only the first sends anything; the rest end with
exit 5 and no worker started.

The comparison itself is the product's update_endpoint_for, called directly.
A test that reimplements the rule checks what the test believes rather than
what the product does.

Also driven: a descriptor naming a different url than the run was given is
refused by the worker rather than resolved in favour of one of them, and a
matching one is accepted with the owner read out of the frame -- not out of
the arguments, which is the whole point of putting it in the frame.

Still missing, and stated in the history rather than implied away: nothing
asserts that the UI stays responsive while the credential wait runs. Moving
it to a thread is visible in the code; "not inline" and "does not block" are
different claims, and asserting the second one needs a test that can drive
the shell's window and message loop.
